transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-29
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Luis Ortega (Redwood Solutions), Maya Thompson (Zephyr Head of AI), Dr. Alan Kerr (Zephyr CTO), Ravi Singh (Zephyr Infra)

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh this is Jordan from Redwood, with Priya and Luis. How's everyone doing?
[00:10] Maya: Doing well, thanks. Excited to see the console walkthrough - we wanted to focus on usage analytics and understanding per-route cost.
[00:18] Jordan: Great, that's exactly what we'll cover. Priya, do you want to kick off the demo?
[00:25] Priya: Yep, jumping in. Pulling up the Redwood console - apologies if the screen shares a little laggy. So top-left is the main usage dashboard, you can see token volume over time, request counts, and an initial cost estimate based on model mix.
[00:45] Dr. Kerr: Is cost here billed per token or is it a blended metric?
[00:50] Priya: We show both. The billing engine uses per-token units per model, but the dashboard gives you route-level aggregated cost so product teams can see which API routes are driving spend. So for example this right-hand pane is per-route breakdown - chat.create, embed.text, rerank - and you can slice by model or by tag.
[01:10] Ravi: When you say route, can we map that to our internal endpoints? We have a single /llm endpoint with a route param in payload.
[01:18] Priya: Yes, you can use tags or route names we pick up from the request metadata. If you send a route header or include a service= tag, it will appear as separate rows in the per-route dashboards. There's also an auto-aggregation mode that heuristically splits flows.
[01:35] Maya: How accurate is token attribution when we have caching and KV cache hits?
[01:40] Priya: Good question - the console differentiates between new token generation and cached prefix hits. Cached hits are visible as separate columns; cost is only attributed to generated tokens, but we show effective latency and hit-rate so you can see both cost savings and latency impact. Sometimes the auto-transcribe labels cache as "KV cache" or "prefetch" - transcription sometimes calls it "KV cash" in older exports, so ignore that - sorry.
[02:05] Jordan: Important to note: in Dedicated and Private modes there's even more visibility - we can surface GPU utilization and per-model kernel-level stats if you'd like to instrument that.
[02:16] Maya: That would be useful for our infra team.
[02:18] Luis: I'll flag that for the follow-up benchmarks.
[02:20] Priya: Now switching to the cost breakdown tab. This is per-token cost columns by model variant - small, base, quantized, and also by A/B rollout. You can see projected monthly spend based on current traffic and the routing policy.
[02:40] Ravi: Can we simulate changes - like if we switch some routes to a quantized variant to save cost, will the console show expected latency degradation?
[02:47] Priya: Yes - we have a "what-if" slider. You pick the route, choose a candidate model (e.g., gptq-7b-qat), and it projects cost change and expected latencies based on our benchmark corpus. It's not perfect but gives a good starting point.
[03:05] Dr. Kerr: Any examples of typical savings?
[03:08] Priya: Sure - for one customer we moved non-critical summaries to a quantized 7B and saved ~38% token cost with a small latency increase. We flagged quality regressions with our eval hooks and rolled back a few prompts.
[03:25] Maya: Eval hooks?
[03:27] Priya: Right, you can attach prompt suites and Redwood will run periodic quality checks and show regression alerts tied to your routes. So if a quantized model starts producing lower scores on your eval set, you'll get an alert.
[03:42] Jordan: On security - Maya mentioned earlier this needs to run in a VPC with customer KMS for keys. We support Private deployment with a customer-managed control plane and KMS/HSM integrations.
[03:55] Ravi: Do you provide audit logs and per-token PII redaction?
[03:59] Jordan: We provide detailed audit trails and integration with SIEM. For PII you can enable masking at the ingestion layer; we also have policies to avoid logging full inputs for Private deployments. SOC 2 reports are available - we'll share the security pack.
[04:15] Maya: Good. Also, want to understand dedicated capacity pricing vs hosted. Can you walk through the numbers?
[04:22] Priya: Sure - I'll pull the pricing tab. Hosted is usage-based - per token model rate. Dedicated is a monthly commit for a GPU pool; you get predictable throughput and lower unit rates for heavy use. The console has an estimator: input your expected qps, average tokens per request, and model mix and it will estimate TCO for hosted vs Dedicated over a 12-month horizon.
[04:48] Ravi: Does the estimator include infra overhead like NVLink utilization or instance preemption?
[04:53] Priya: It models effective throughput based on observed kernel performance; for Dedicated we include provisioning inefficiencies and we show a confidence band. For very spiky workloads we recommend a hybrid: Dedicated for baseline and hosted burst.
[05:08] Maya: Can we export the per-route cost CSV to our FinOps tools?
[05:12] Priya: Yes - export or connect via API. We can also stream usage events to your data lake for custom analysis.
[05:19] Dr. Kerr: About latency SLOs - if we set a 200ms SLO, how do routing policies help?
[05:25] Priya: Smart routing can favor lower-latency model variants or regionally closer capacity. The console's route config page lets you set policies per route - prefer low-latency, prefer low-cost, or fallbacks to cheaper variants. It will simulate expected SLO attainment given current capacity.
[05:45] Luis: There's also a fallback chain you can define - e.g., try model A, if capacity full route to model B, else to hosted.
[05:53] Maya: For compliance we need data residency in EU for some routes. Is per-route residency control possible?
[05:58] Priya: Yes, you can pin routes to regions - either at the route metadata level or via routing policy. Private deployments give you full control. Hosted can be region-restricted as well if we have capacity in the region.
[06:12] Ravi: For the POC we want to run a benchmark with our prompt set and measure cost vs latency. What's the timeline?
[06:18] Jordan: If you can share sample traffic and SLOs by next week, Priya and Luis will set up a bench and run both hosted and Dedicated profiles.
[06:24] Maya: We can do that.
[06:25] Priya: Quick note on instrumentation - include 1) sample prompts 2) expected qps and burst pattern 3) success criteria (latency, hallucination threshold). We'll produce a report with per-route dashboards and a cost delta table.
[06:40] Dr. Kerr: Are there any gotchas with model quantization for medical text?
[06:44] Priya: Medical domain sometimes needs higher-precision models; quantization can reduce quality in niche terminology. That's why we use eval suites pre- and post-quant to catch regressions. Also you can do partial quantization for non-critical routes.
[06:58] Maya: Ok makes sense.
[07:00] Jordan: We're about 40 minutes in - want to do a quick recap and next steps.
[07:04] Priya: Recap: 1) Console shows per-route dashboards with token-level attribution and cache-hit visibility. 2) Cost estimator and what-if tool for model swaps. 3) Routing policies for latency/cost/residency. 4) Eval hooks and regression alerts. 5) Private/Dedicated options for tighter control and lower unit costs at scale.
[07:25] Jordan: Next steps: Jordan will send Dedicated pricing + pilot proposal; Priya will share benchmark plan and sample prompt guide; Ravi will provide sample traffic profile and SLOs. Aim to schedule POC demo for Private deployment in week of Oct 12.
[07:40] Maya: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[07:43] Dr. Kerr: Thanks, helpful session.
[07:46] Jordan: Thanks all - we'll follow up with the deck and security pack.
[07:50] [call ends]

Notes: transcription has minor mislabels and occasional filler words; product names sometimes abbreviated (e.g., "KV cache" shows as "KV cash" in some auto exports).
